Indian Standard
HOROLOGY -- WATCH STRAPS
PART 3 SOLID LINK STRAPS -- SPECIFICATION

1 SCOPE This standard (Part 3) specifies the dimensions, material, general requirements and tests of solid link straps. 2 REFERENCE The following standard contains provision which through reference in this text, constitutes provision of this standard. At the time of publication, the edition indicated was valid. All standards are subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on this standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent edition of the standard indicated below: IS No, 10865:1998 Title Wrist watches -- Spring bars for watch cases and straps -- Specification

5 CONSTRUCTION 5.1 The different elements of the solid link watch straps may be manufactured by press operations or by machining. The solid links are joined together by pin: in predetermined pattem/design to achieve the final shape. 5.2 The clearance between link, linking pinlhead of screw or snap pinto be minimum 50 micrometres. The maximum value shall depend upon design of bracelet. 5.3 The head of the linking pinlhead of screw or snap pin shall not protrude from the side of the links. 5.4 There shall be provision strap length. Adjustability 1) 2) range: mm, 210 to 150 mm for adjustability of the

NOTE --

Clasp connectors are designed to connect clasp

and to simulate the pattern of solid link

FIG. 3 CLASPCONNECmRS AND PIN 6.1.2 The linking pin can be any other type but shall satisfi the functional requirements (see Fig. 4). 7 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 7.1 Strap Body The joints shall be such that the intermediate gap between two links is just sufficient to have the required flexibility of strap. This working gap shall be uniform throughout the length of the strap. There shall be no abnormal play between links. 7.2 Watch Catch

For catch width215 (along with case)

For catch width< 15 mm, 180 to 140 mm

6 D1MENS1ONS 6.1 Solid Link and Clasp Connection 6.1.1 The strap width FVz as shown in Fig. 2 and 3 shall preferably be 6,8, 10, 12, 14,16,18 and20 mm or maybe different depending upon the construction/look of the strap. There shall be no abnormal play or loose linkage between the watch catch and the main strap. There shall be a provision for removal of the spring bars or linking pins from the watch case. 7.3 Strap Clasp 7.3.1 There shall be no abnormal play in the joints between the strap body and the clasp. The clasp and lock assembly shall be free from sharp edges and burrs. w ~ 7.3.2 Clasp assembly shall be marked legibly and indelibly with the source of manufacture or registered trade-mark.

IS 13718 (Part 3):2002 construction, dimensions, general requirements, workmanship and finish (see 4,5, 6,7 and 8) shall meet the following test requirements. 9.1.2 The complete strap assembly shall withstand an axial/suspended load of minimum 98.1 N (10 kgf) without any noticeable change in the original condition of strap assembly like opening of links and original length of strap, etc. 9.1.3 Loosening torque of the screw shall be greater than 0.015 N.m (150 g.cm) but less than 0.039 N.m (400 g.cm).
in millimetres.

AH dimensions

FIG. 9 SUPPORTPIN and de-clasping force shall be 1.5 to 2.5 kgf 1)and 1.0 to 1.5 kgf, respectively, for straps with catch width equal toor greater than 15mmandl.Oto 2.0 kgf and 0,8 to 1.3 kgf, respectively, for straps with catch width less than 15 mm. 7.4 Spring Bars The spring bars shall not project more than 0.2 mm outside the clasp. There shall be no abnormal play between the spring bar pin and the hole in the clasp. Other details of spring bars shall conform to IS 10865. 7.5 Linking Pins All the linking pins used in clasp and strap body shall remain in position and shall not come out during normal usage. 8 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH
7.3.3 Clasping

9.2 Torque and Twist Connect one end of strap to the torque meter and apply a torque of 0.20 N.m (2 kgf.cm) by twisting the strap at the free end. The strap shall withstand the test without any deformation and loosening. 9.3 Flexibility Each half of the strap shall at least form a semicircle when folded in the direction of normal usage of strap. The strap shall be uniformly flexible over its entire length and there shall not be any hugging at the catch or any part of the strap. 10 PACKING Each strap shall be put in a polythene cover and such of those straps having the same catch width and same design shall be packed in a cardboard box in 100 numbers. 11 MARKING 11.1 Each cardboard box shall have marking for catch width, design and the quantity of straps. 11.2 BIS Certification Marking The product may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 11.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the rules and regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the Iicence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers maybe obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.

8.1 All the sharp edges and corners shall be ground and polished to have a smooth finish. The finish of the strap shall be as agreed to between the manufacturer and the buyer. 8.2 All the straps shall be thoroughly and properly cleaned to ensure that these are totally free from buffing and polishing compounds. 9 TESTS 9.1 Pull-Off Force 9.1.1 The strap assembly apart from material,
